meta.title: Asian LNG supply network, 2025 baseline

diversion.note: Share of each exporter's non-Asian (mainly European) cargoes that Asian buyers can bid away in a crisis. No direct source; varied 0-50% in robustness checks. Chosen by the author with the user (stage 2).

horizon_days.note: Crisis length used to convert storage inventory into a sustainable withdrawal rate in buffered λ (inventory × 365 / 90). Varied in robustness checks.

source_notes.GIIGNL: GIIGNL Annual Report 2026 data were read from the public PDF copy at https://www.worldlngsummit.com/media/5stjrkng/2026-giignl-annual-report.pdf (giignl.org gates downloads to members). Page references refer to that PDF.
source_notes.EI: Energy Institute Statistical Review of World Energy 2026 data workbook (EI-Stats-Review-ALL-data.xlsx), sheets 'Gas trade 2025 - pipeline', 'Gas - LNG imports bcm', 'Gas inputs - Elec generation'. Used for China's pipeline imports and as a cross-check on GIIGNL LNG imports (agree within ~1% except Korea, ~5% lower in EI) and on fuel-switching scale.

notes: Gas is pooled and fungible: any cargo can serve any importer reachable by a path. Contracts, prices and destination clauses are not modeled.
Rates are annualised (mtpa). A closure is assumed to last long enough that annual rates are meaningful; storage converts to days of cover.

36.7 bcm/yr. Modeled capacity = 2025 flow. EI Statistical Review 2026, 'Gas trade 2025 - pipeline': Russia → China 36.7 bcm. Other estimates are higher (Kpler 39.2, TASS ~38.8); the pipe is at or near its 38 bcm design, so little headroom.

design_capacity.note: 38 bcm/yr design capacity (Global Energy Monitor, Global Gas Infrastructure Tracker). Reference only.

capacity.note: 36.7 bcm/yr. Modeled capacity = 2025 flow. EI 2026: Turkmenistan 30.3 + Kazakhstan 4.9 + Uzbekistan 1.5 bcm into China (Kpler implies ~36.7, consistent). Supply-limited, not pipe-limited: Lines A-C can carry 55 bcm but Central Asian producers are diverting gas home; Line D (30 bcm) is still proposed.

design_capacity.note: 55 bcm/yr design capacity (Global Energy Monitor, Global Gas Infrastructure Tracker). Reference only.

capacity.note: 4.4 bcm/yr. Modeled capacity = 2025 flow. EI 2026: Myanmar → China 4.4 bcm (Kpler 4.8). Limited by Shwe field output, not by the pipe.

design_capacity.note: 12 bcm/yr design capacity (Global Energy Monitor, Global Gas Infrastructure Tracker). Reference only.

capacity.note: 4.4 bcm/yr. Modeled capacity = 2025 flow. EPPO Table 3.1-1, 2025 average imports: Yadana 174 + Yetagun 28 + Zawtika 220 = 422 MMSCFD (1,000 Btu/scf). EI 2026 cross-check: 4.2 bcm. Fields are depleting.

0.0 bcm/yr. Modeled capacity = 2025 flow. Proposed (GEM: 2030 start). Legally binding construction agreement signed Sept 2025, but route and price unresolved. Modeled at zero so the investment ranking can test building it.

import_demand.note: 2025 LNG imports by source 65.7 Mt (GIIGNL trade matrix, gross of reloads). Demand that must be met by imports. Cross-check: EI Statistical Review 2026 reports 88.5 bcm of 2025 LNG imports (≈65.1 Mt).

inventory.note: National LNG inventories 'just under four million tonnes' (METI statement reported by Reuters, week to 8 Mar 2026). METI's own weekly series covers power utilities only: 2.20 Mt on 1 Mar 2026 (https://www.enecho.meti.go.jp/category/electricity_and_gas/electricity_measures/pdf/denryoku_LNG_stock.pdf). City-gas stocks make up the rest.

max_withdrawal.note: Tank LNG is sent out through the regas vaporizers, so withdrawal is limited by regas capacity (and shares it with arriving cargoes).

fuel_switch.note: IEA GMR Q2-2026: lifting operational restrictions on coal plants saves ~0.5 Mt LNG/yr; Kashiwazaki-Kariwa 6 (1.36 GW) entering commercial operation mid-April 2026 ≈ 1.36 × 0.8 × 8,760 h ≈ 9.5 TWh ≈ 1.2 Mt. Sum ~1.7, rounded to 2. Oil-fired backup excluded because oil is also short in a Hormuz closure. (Was 3.0 before source upgrade.) Scale check: EI 2026 gas-fired generation 308.8 TWh ≈ 39 Mt LNG-eq of power-sector gas burn, so this is ~5% of it.

inventory.note: Underground storage 16.8 bcm at end-Feb 2026 (CGEP) = 12.4 Mt, consistent with IGU's 19.8 bcm working-gas capacity (Oct 2025); plus LNG tanks at an assumed 50% fill (27.9 M m3 × 0.45 t/m3 × 50% = 6.3 Mt).

max_withdrawal.note: Peak underground-storage withdrawal. No national figure is published (IGU reports capacity, not deliverability); facility data such as Wen23 (39 mcm/d for 4 bcm working gas, ~1% of working gas per day) scaled to China's 19.8 bcm gives ~0.2 bcm/d. Estimate 60 mtpa ≈ 0.22 bcm/d.

fuel_switch.note: IEA GMR Q2-2026: China's LNG imports fell 30% y-o-y in March 2026 and its 60-65 bcm regional switching estimate explicitly includes China; CGEP: Guangdong cut gas burn to 56-70% of its 2025 rate. Estimate ~20 bcm/yr (15 Mt) nationally. Scale check: EI 2026 gas-fired generation 337.6 TWh ≈ 43 Mt LNG-eq of power-sector gas burn, so this is ~35% of it.
